description:
Eurostat's circularity headline indicator: the share of material
recycled and fed back into the economy as a fraction of total material
use. The only officially compiled, openly licensed, machine-readable
circularity-share series in existence.
license: Eurostat re-use policy (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU) — free re-use with attribution
name: Eurostat — Circular Material Use Rate (cei_srm030)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 with a live call:
?format=JSON&lang=EN&time=2023&geo=ES returned Spain 2023 = 8.2%.
Coverage 2004-2023, annual, updated late in the year (last 2025-11-24).
WHY THIS MATTERS DISPROPORTIONATELY: the framework's 'circular economy
share' indicator has no global open source. The Circularity Gap Report
headline (7.2% circular) is a PDF number with no underlying dataset, no
licence and no methodology download, and the Ellen MacArthur Foundation
publishes frameworks and case studies rather than data. This Eurostat
series is the only real machine-readable circularity share anywhere -
and it is EU-only and material-based rather than GDP-based. For a global
figure the index must compute its own from OECD material flow accounts
or EXIOBASE and say so.

description:
Eurostat's official green-jobs account: employment in full-time
equivalents, value added and output for the environmental goods and
services sector, split by NACE industry and CEPA/CReMA environmental
purpose, for EU and EFTA countries.
license: Eurostat re-use policy (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU) — free re-use with attribution, equivalent to CC-BY-4.0
name: Eurostat — Environmental Goods and Services Sector (EGSS)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 with a live call returning real values: Spain 2022,
nace_r2=TOTAL, ceparema=TOTAL, ty=TOT_EGSS gave 547,585 FTE; nace_r2=C
(Manufacturing), ceparema=TOT_CEPA gave 267,586 FTE. Dataset 'Employment
in the environmental goods and services sector (2000-2023)', 920,908
observations, updated 2025-06-05. The databrowser web page is a JS shell
and returns nothing - the API is the only usable path. GOTCHA: wrong
dimension codes return {"value":{}} silently with HTTP 200 rather than
an error. ceparema=TOTAL_CEPA_CREMA and na_item=EMP both returned empty.
Use ceparema=TOTAL, ty=TOT_EGSS, unit=FTE. SLICING: geo= country level,
EU27 plus EFTA and candidates, no NUTS2 in this table. EU-ONLY - no
coverage for the Boston, Santiago or Bali pilots. Also the best
available proxy for 'regenerative business growth' via EGSS output and
value added as a share of the economy.

description:
Global multi-regional environmentally extended input-output database
covering 44 countries plus 5 rest-of-world regions and 163 industries,
with employment, material, land and emissions satellite accounts
alongside monetary flows.
license: CC-BY-SA-4.0 for v3.8.2 — NOTE v3.9.6 and later are non-commercial only, see notes
name: EXIOBASE 3 — multi-regional environmentally extended input-output tables
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09. THIS ENTRY DELIBERATELY PINS v3.8.2 (Zenodo record
5589597, 1995-2022, 49.4 GB), because the licence narrowed in later
releases. v3.8.2 states 'provided free of charge to users under a CC-BY-
SA license'. v3.9.6 (record 15689391, published 2025-06-18, 1995-2020
core with now-cast to 2022, beta v3.10 to 2024, 28.1 GB) is dual-
licensed: CC-BY-SA-NC derivative for non-commercial and academic use,
with a commercial licence still 'under development' (contact exiobase-
support@googlegroups.com). If PLANETAI has any commercial surface, use
v3.8.2 and document why; v3.9.6 did fix employment account bugs, so
weigh that against the licence. Standard reader is the pymrio Python
package. STRONGEST SPATIAL ANSWER IN THE ECONOMIC ROW: 49 regions with
consumption-based accounting, so a bioregion's true economic draw
including imports is derivable rather than just its territorial
production. Sub-country requires your own regionalisation. Also the
licence-clean substitute for UN Comtrade, which prohibits re-
dissemination without permission and caps free apps at 100,000 records.

description:
FAO Food Balance Sheets: production, imports, exports, stock change,
feed, seed, losses and food supply per commodity per country. The
canonical basis for any food self-sufficiency ratio.
license: CC-BY-4.0 (FAO standard database licence — not confirmable from the pages fetched; verify at download)
name: FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 by existence: https://bulks-
faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data_(Normalized).zip
returned a 413 response-too-large, which confirms the file serves. DO
NOT PROMISE AN API. Three endpoints were tested and all failed:
faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1 returned 401, fenixservices.fao.org
returned HTTP 521 (origin down), bulks-
faostat.fao.org/production/datasets_en.json returned 403. FAO announced
a new developer portal but it requires sign-in and publishes no public
base URL. Build the food self-sufficiency connector on bulk download
plus local parse, with Our World in Data as the fallback mirror. Self-
sufficiency ratio = production / (production + imports - exports) per
commodity. Coverage: FBS 2010-2023 under the new methodology, old series
1961-2013, annual release around December, roughly 245 countries and
territories. SLICING: country table, normalized long CSV, national only.
A bioregion crossing borders or smaller than a country needs
downscaling.

description:
Economy-wide material flow accounts published by the UN
International Resource Panel. National-level material extraction,
imports, exports, consumption by category.
name: materialflows.net (UN International Resource Panel)
notes:
Methodologically aligned with Eurostat EW-MFA. Used as the
baseline for the PLANETAI HS->material crosswalk (Wave 16).
No API; bulk Excel + CSV downloads. Updated annually.
The most globally consistent MFA dataset; combine with
Eurostat for higher EU resolution.

description:
OECD's green growth indicator set delivered over a public SDMX REST API
with no key. Carries green jobs, environmental goods and services trade,
environmental taxation, fossil-fuel support and resource productivity
for OECD and partner economies.
license: OECD terms — CC-BY-4.0 for most OECD statistical data, not restated on the SDMX endpoint; verify per dataflow
name: OECD Green Growth Indicators (SDMX)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 with a live call returning JSON observations for
Spain; dimension metadata exposes 157 measures including green jobs,
environmental goods trade, environmental taxes and subsidies, material
consumption, energy and GHG productivity, environmental R&D budgets and
protected areas. Dataflow discovery verified: 51 dataflows under
OECD.ENV.EPI. Documentation references an August 2026 release. Coverage
roughly 1990-2023 depending on measure. IMPORTANT: the older
www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/green-growth-indicators*.html landing
pages 404'd on two spellings - use the SDMX endpoint, never the web
page. SLICING: SDMX key, first position is REF_AREA ISO3
(ESP.............. returns all measures for Spain). Country resolution
only.

description:
OECD economy-wide material flow accounts by material category covering
metals, non-metallic minerals, biomass and fossil energy carriers.
Includes domestic material consumption and material footprint, the
consumption-based measure needed for honest circularity accounting.
license: OECD terms — CC-BY-4.0 for most OECD statistical data, not restated on the endpoint
name: OECD Material Flow Accounts (SDMX)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 with a live call on
DSD_MATERIAL_RESOURCES@DF_MATERIAL_RESOURCES returning JSON for
2020-2025. Eight measures confirmed: domestic extraction used, imports,
exports, physical trade balance, direct material input, domestic
material consumption, material footprint, share in total DMC. Coverage
roughly 1990-2025 with recent years now-cast, annual. OVERLAP NOTE: this
partially duplicates materialflows.net (UN IRP), which is already in the
list. They are complements not duplicates - materialflows.net has longer
coverage (1970-2024) and more countries (200+), OECD has the API. Keep
both and prefer the IRP series for long time series, OECD for
programmatic access. SLICING: SDMX key first position is ISO3 country.
National only.

description:
UN Statistics Division's environmental-economic accounting programme.
Currently a country-implementation tracker plus an Excel questionnaire
collection; a compiled global account database is announced but not yet
published.
name: UN SEEA Global Data Collection
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 and deliberately filed as PLANNED, not live. It is a
data submission framework, not a data portal: Excel questionnaires with
macros for Physical Energy Flow Accounts and Air Emission Accounts, with
submissions due 30 September 2026. UNSD states that submitted data 'will
be validated and then disseminated through a database maintained by
UNSD' - that database does not exist yet. The 2025 Global Assessment
confirms 98 countries have implemented SEEA and 71 of them (72%) publish
at least one account regularly, published as per-country PDF reports
2020-2025. ACTION: set a re-check for Q1 2027. This is the source that
would eventually make SEEA-based natural capital and circularity
accounting official rather than improvised, and it would materially
improve the economic bioregion row.

description:
World Bank register of carbon taxes and emissions trading systems
worldwide with prices, coverage and revenues by jurisdiction, at both
national and sub-national level. Companion to the annual State and
Trends of Carbon Pricing report.
name: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09. 121 instruments, revenue series 1990-2025,
irregular refresh. DOWNLOAD PATH IS DEGRADED: /compliance/data-download
returned 404 and the Excel path found via search (data_08_2025.xlsx)
also 404'd - do not use it. The /map_data view renders but exposes no
download link and shows 'last updated March 31, 2023'. Scrape the
dashboard or contact data@worldbank.org for the file. RARE SUB-NATIONAL
RESOLUTION: instruments are recorded at national and sub-national level
(California, Quebec and similar), so some bioregions map directly onto a
single instrument - one of only two sources in the economic row that
breaks below the nation-state. INDICATOR CAVEAT: carbon pricing revenue
is a state-levied environmental payment, not a payments-for-ecosystem-
services scheme. Use it explicitly labelled as a proxy for PES, or not
at all.

description:
World Bank wealth accounts measuring produced, human and natural capital
as stocks per country. The only globally consistent open natural-capital
valuation series, machine-readable through the Data360 API.
name: World Bank Changing Wealth of Nations (CWON)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 with a live call:
?DATABASE_ID=WB_CWON&REF_AREA=ESP&timePeriodFrom=2018&timePeriodTo=2020
returned 366 JSON records across indicators WB_CWON_NW_TOW (total
wealth), _NW_NFL (natural capital), _NW_HCA (human capital), _NW_PCA
(per capita) and _NW_NFA (net foreign assets), in real chained 2019 USD
and current USD, at both per-capita and total aggregation. CWON 2024
methodology, 1995-2020, 151 countries, annual, published roughly every
3-4 years (2018, 2021, 2024). API CAVEAT: data360.worldbank.org/en/api
returned only a beta shell page with no rendered documentation. The
endpoint works but is undocumented and in beta - pin your query shapes
and expect breakage. SLICING: country only, no sub-national; a bioregion
is an aggregation of country rows and sub-country natural capital would
require downscaling.

description:
Two complementary Barcelona business registers: a census of ground-floor
commercial premises by activity, and the padro of the economic activities
tax (IAE) by activity type. Together a business-density signal.
name: Barcelona - Cens d'activitat economica i padro de l'IAE
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 1). Dataset ids:
cens-locals-planta-baixa-act-economica and rebuts-quota-padro-iae. Both
CC-BY-4.0 via the CKAN action API.

TWO DIFFERENT REGISTERS, DELIBERATELY IN ONE ENTRY. The premises census
counts physical ground-floor units and what each is used for; the IAE padro
counts taxable economic activities. They answer "how much commerce is on the
street" and "how much activity is declared" respectively, and neither alone
is a business registry in the usual sense.

The premises dataset page carries its own methodology caveat - read it before
using counts as a time series.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: there is no GDP-per-capita, no R&D and no circular-economy
dataset at city scale on this portal. A combined CKAN query for those returned
nothing in the wave-1 pass, though single-term Catalan retries were not made,
so treat the cell as under-searched rather than proven empty.

description:
Ajuntament de Barcelona publishes its municipal budget and its settled
execution as annual CSV series - revenue and expenditure, planned (inicial)
and liquidated, by chapter, article and programme.
name: Barcelona - Pressupost municipal i execucio
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 1) via the CKAN action
API. Every dataset fetched returned license_title "Creative Commons
Attribution 4.0".

BOTH SIDES OF THE LEDGER, BOTH STATES: verified dataset ids -
evolucio-resultat-ingressos-i-despeses, evolucio-ingressos-per-capitols,
evolucio-ingressos-per-capitols-i-articles, evolucio-despeses-per-capitols,
evolucio-despeses-per-capitols-i-articles,
evolucio-despeses-corrents-per-politiques,
evolucio-despeses-per-unitats-organiques, modificacions-credit-pressupost
(execution / credit modifications, 9 CSVs spanning 2017-2025), and
l01080193-presupuestos-consolidados-de-la-ciudad-de-barcelona-iniciales-segun-lgep-y-loepsf
(initial consolidated, 2016-2025).

CLASSIFICATION: Spanish local-entity chart of accounts - capitol / article /
concepte on the economic axis, politica / programa on the functional axis.
No COFOG crosswalk is stated on any dataset page. The politica/programa axis
is the crosswalkable one if a mapping is ever built.

GRANULARITY IS CHAPTER-LEVEL, NOT LINE-ITEM. Liquidated series are expressed
in millions of euros. Compare with Rennes in the France wave, which publishes
~600 records per year at true line-item granularity - Barcelona is coarser.

Fiscal year = calendar year. Coverage 2008/2016-2025 depending on series.
EUR, nominal. Annual cadence; catalogue metadata_modified 2026-06-09.

FEDERATABLE: the INE municipality code is carried inside the catalogue
identifier itself - L01080193 = L01 (ayuntamiento) + 08019 (INE) + check
digit. That is the join key to the Ministerio de Hacienda aggregate local
series.

ACCESS CAVEAT: every human-facing HTML page on this portal sits behind a
BunkerWeb/hCaptcha bot challenge. Only /data/api/action/* JSON is machine
accessible. Do not build anything that scrapes the dataset pages.

description:
City of Boston five-year capital investment plan, FY27-31, roughly 4.4 billion
USD, published as bulk CSV with a PDF data dictionary and refreshed annually.
license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL)
name: Boston - Capital Plan
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 1).

NOT SPATIALLY DISAGGREGATED. Every row is geo-tagged "Boston (all)" - there
is no neighbourhood or census-tract breakdown. That matters because the
capital plan is the one municipal dataset that would naturally answer
"where is money being spent", and here it cannot.

This is also why the community rung of the budget ladder is empty for Boston:
a search of the portal for tract or neighbourhood finance, including
participatory-budgeting allocations, found nothing. Recorded as checked-empty
in the coverage tracker, not as unchecked.

description:
Actual executed City of Boston expenditure by vendor and department,
transaction level, published as per-fiscal-year CSVs from FY2012 onward and
refreshed monthly.
license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL)
name: Boston - Checkbook Explorer
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 1). Per-FY CSVs
FY2012-present, current through May 2025 at time of check. Monthly cadence.

TRANSACTION-LEVEL EXECUTED SPEND, MONTHLY. This is the best fiscal-execution
source found anywhere in wave 1 - finer and fresher than Barcelona's
chapter-level annual liquidation and than anything available for Bali or
Santiago. If the Index ever wants an executed-vs-planned ratio computed
honestly, Boston is where the method should be prototyped.

EXCLUDES PAYROLL by design. Pair with /dataset/employee-earnings-report
(individual-level earnings, CSV/XLSX, 2011-2025, annual) for the full
outturn. Neither is complete alone and the two do not overlap.

No consolidated ACFR/CAFR data file was found on the portal - the audited
statements exist as PDF volumes on boston.gov, not as open data.

Same FIPS/GEOID absence as the budget files: internal department codes only.

description:
City of Boston adopted operating budget and revenue budget, published as
bulk CSV with a PDF data dictionary, by department and programme for the
General Fund.
license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL)
name: Boston - Operating and Revenue Budget
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 1). Two datasets:
/dataset/operating-budget (planned expenditure) and /dataset/revenue-budget
(planned revenue). FY27 Adopted is current; budget documents run back to
FY2011 on boston.gov.

PLANNED ONLY. Executed spending is a separate publication - see
boston-checkbook-explorer in this registry. Payroll actuals are separate
again (/dataset/employee-earnings-report, individual-level, 2011-2025), and
Checkbook explicitly excludes them, so the three together are the complete
fiscal picture and no two of them overlap.

Fiscal year runs 1 July to 30 June. USD, nominal. Granularity is
programme-within-department.

FEDERATION PROBLEM, RECORDED DELIBERATELY: these files carry the City's own
internal department and programme codes and NO FIPS/GEOID. Boston's place
code is 2507000 and it appears nowhere in the budget data. There is no
crosswalk to the state (CTHRU) or federal (USAspending) rungs without
building one. Any comparison across US localities hits this first.

Classification is the City's own chart of accounts; no COFOG crosswalk found.

ACCESS CAVEAT: data.boston.gov robots.txt disallows /api/, so the CKAN action
API cannot be used by a well-behaved client. Bulk CSV download only. The
api field is null for that reason, not because no endpoint exists.

description:
City of Cambridge capital budget project funding by fiscal year, FY2020 to
FY2031, with per-project latitude and longitude for each funded capital
project.
license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL)
name: Cambridge - Capital budget
notes:
Verified 2026-09-10 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 7, United States).
data_updated_at 2026-05-05. Twelve-year forward window FY2020-FY2031.

GEOCODED PER PROJECT. Columns: approved_amount, fiscal_year, department,
project_name, project_id, fund, city_location, latitude, longitude,
map_location. This is the only capital plan in wave 7 with per-project
coordinates, and it is materially better than Boston's, which is geo-tagged
"Boston (all)" with no breakdown.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THE INDEX: coordinates make this the one wave-7 source
that can be aggregated to a sub-city rung without an admin-code crosswalk.
Spatial join to census tract or neighbourhood is possible directly. If the
FCI wants a community-scale public-finance signal for a US locality, this is
the prototype - not the budget files, which have no geography at all.

Fiscal year 1 Jul - 30 Jun. USD nominal. Approved/planned amounts only, no
execution against them.

description:
City of Cambridge annual operating budget as two paired Socrata datasets -
budgeted revenues by source and budgeted expenditures by department and
division - covering FY2011 to FY2027.
license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL)
name: Cambridge - Operating budget, revenues and expenditures
notes:
Verified 2026-09-10 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 7, United States).

TWO DATASETS, ONE SOURCE. Revenues: /d/ixyv-mje6, columns category,
service, fiscal_year, department_name, description, amount, fund.
Expenditures: /d/5bn4-5wey, same shape plus division_name. Both carried
data_updated_at 2026-09-08 at time of check - the freshest municipal budget
data found anywhere in wave 7. Both run FY2011-FY2027, a 17-year continuous
series.

LICENCE INCONSISTENCY WITHIN ONE SOURCE: the revenues dataset states
"Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License"; the expenditures
dataset states plain "Public Domain". Both are open, but a harvester keying
on an exact licence string will split this pair.

PLANNED ONLY, NOT EXECUTED. These are appropriations. No liquidation /
outturn file was found, so unlike Boston's Checkbook Explorer there is no
executed-spend counterpart here. Budgeted salaries sit separately at
/d/ixg8-tyau (PDDL, per-FY views back to FY2024) and are the closest thing
to an actuals series.

SAME FEDERATION PROBLEM AS BOSTON: the files carry department, division,
service and fund codes and NO FIPS/GEOID. Cambridge place code 2511000
(verified on census.gov QuickFacts) appears nowhere in the data. Joining
this to the Commonwealth or federal rung requires a crosswalk that does not
exist yet.

Fiscal year 1 Jul - 30 Jun. USD nominal. Granularity: line item within
department/division. No COFOG crosswalk. Access tier: SODA API plus bulk
CSV - better than Boston, which is bulk CSV only.

description:
Kota Denpasar publishes its annual budget summaries and RKPD-to-APBD
consistency documents as CKAN datasets, mostly from BPKAD, in CSV with a
public-domain licence.
name: Kota Denpasar - APBD (Ringkasan dan konsistensi RKPD-APBD)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 1). Query "APBD"
returned 29 datasets, publisher mostly BPKAD (22 of them), 26 in CSV and 2
PDF, fiscal years 2022-2025.

THE ONLY OPENLY LICENSED INDONESIAN FISCAL SOURCE FOUND. Licence verbatim
"Lainnya (Domain Publik)" on all 29. Every other route to Indonesian public
finance carries a bare copyright notice and no grant - see the coverage
tracker's restricted-licence list, which includes the DJPK SIKD portal that
holds anggaran and realisasi for all 546 pemda and is therefore the single
most valuable Indonesian fiscal source and unusable under CONTRIBUTING
criterion 1.

SUMMARIES, NOT EXECUTION. These are Ringkasan APBD - budget summaries. For
anggaran against realisasi you need DJPK, which is the unlicensed source
above. So Denpasar is openly licensed and coarse, while the fine-grained
execution data exists and cannot be used. That trade is the finding.

ADMIN CODE: Kota Denpasar is Kemendagri 51.71 (BPS 5171), Provinsi Bali 51,
ISO 3166-2 ID-BA. Note that DJPK uses its own "kode pemda" which was NOT
confirmed identical to the Kemendagri code - resolve before joining
Indonesian fiscal data across sources.

The CKAN action API is documented in the portal footer but package_search was
blocked by robots.txt in this pass, so the dataset counts above come from
rendered facets. CKAN 2.8.3.

description:
Full DGFiP accounting balances for every French commune, covering principal and
ancillary budgets (budgets principaux et budgets annexes), published yearly by
the French finance ministry as CSV, JSON and ZIP.
name: DGFiP Balances comptables des communes
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 2, France). Landing page
returned HTTP 200; publisher "Ministeres economiques et financiers" with DGFIP
as editor; licence "Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0" verbatim.
Formats offered: CSV, JSON, ZIP (95.8 Mo) and two ODF spreadsheets.

This is the EXECUTION side of the French city budget rung and the reason it is
a separate entry from the comptes individuels: balances comptables are the
account-by-account movements actually recorded, where comptes individuels are
the summarised annual accounts. Both are needed to answer "planned vs executed"
for a French commune.

Covers budgets annexes as well as the principal budget - important because
French cities push water, waste, transport and social action into annexes, so a
principal-budget-only reading understates municipal spend.

Classification is the national chart of accounts (M14/M52/M57 account numbers).
No COFOG crosswalk published.

Yearly datasets, one per exercice (2019 ... 2024 all confirmed present on the
portal). data.gouv.fr rates this dataset's own metadata quality "A ameliorer
(44 %)" - the data is fine, the metadata is thin, so fiscal-year convention and
update cadence have to be read off the file structure document rather than the
dataset page.

description:
Accounting balances of French intercommunal groupings (EPCI — métropoles, communautés
d'agglomération, communautés de communes), 2010 onward, from DGFiP. The only open source
covering the EPCI fiscal tier nationally.
name: DGFiP — Balances comptables des groupements à fiscalité propre depuis 2010
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09: dataset page and API metadata opened, HTTP 200. Last update 2026-07-13.
WHY THIS MATTERS FOR FAB CITY: several French Fab City members are EPCIs, not communes —
Valence Romans Agglo (SIREN 200068781), Toulouse Métropole (243100518), Rennes Métropole,
Métropole du Grand Paris. For those members the commune-level DGFiP files miss the tier that
actually holds the waste, water, transport and economic-development budgets. This file is the
only open national source that covers it.
SCALE TENSION, FLAGGED NOT HIDDEN: filed at scale "city" because the FCI Regime 1 convention
admits only city and region, and the EPCI is the member's own operating tier. Its true
resolution is inter-municipal, between the two. Revisit if the taxonomy gains that rung.
Covers budgets principaux and budgets annexes; from 2017 it also includes établissements
publics territoriaux. 2019-2025 available as export, all years from 2010 in the "Balance_GFP"
attachments.
Join key is SIREN, not INSEE — different key from the commune files, which is a real
integration cost when combining the two tiers.
Classification: national chart of accounts. NOT COFOG, no crosswalk. EUR, nominal.
Fiscal year = calendar exercice.

description:
DGFiP annual individual accounts for every French commune, published as one
global file per year cohort on the Ministry of Finance open-data portal.
Carries revenue, expenditure, debt and balance-sheet aggregates per commune.
name: DGFiP Comptes individuels des communes (fichier global)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 2, France). Landing page
returned HTTP 200 and states producer "Ministere de l'Economie, des Finances et
de la Souverainete industrielle, energetique et numerique" and licence
"Licence Ouverte 2.0" verbatim.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR FEDERATION: this is the single source that gives the city
budget rung for EVERY French Fab City member at once - Brest (INSEE 29019),
Montpellier (34172), Paris (75056), Rennes (35238), Toulouse (31555) - keyed on
the commune code. No per-city portal visit is required to fill the city budget
cell in France.

Published as year-cohort datasets (2023-2024, 2022, 2021, 2017 ... each a
separate dataset id), not one continuous series, so a time series requires
stitching cohorts.

Classification is the French national chart of accounts for local authorities
(M14/M52 up to 2017, M57 from 2018), NOT COFOG. No COFOG crosswalk is published
alongside; the functional ("fonction"/"sous-fonction") axis is the closest
bridge and exists only in some collectivites' own publications.

Granularity is aggregate-to-chapter per commune, not line item. For line-item
detail use the city's own portal (Paris, Rennes and Toulouse all publish it).

The data.gouv.fr copy titled "Comptes individuels des communes" is a
third-party reupload by an individual contributor, last updated 2018 and
flagged "Frequence de mise a jour non respectee" - treat that one as stale and
use this ministry-published cohort series instead.

description: Japan's full-coverage census of every business establishment and enterprise, giving number of establishments, employees and sales by industry down to municipality level. Survey reference June 2021, published 2023-06-27, updated through December 2025.
license: 政府標準利用規約（第2.0版）- explicitly CC BY 4.0 compatible
name: Japan 2021 Economic Census for Business Activity (経済センサス-活動調査)
notes:

name: Paris - Etats speciaux d'arrondissement (sub-municipal budgets)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 2, France). Confirmed
dataset ids in the Paris catalogue, all ODbL:
budgets-votes-etats-speciaux-darrondissements (2009-2017),
budgets-votes-etats-speciaux-darrondissements-m57-ville (from 2018), and
comptes-administratifs-etats-speciaux-darrondissement (executed).

SCALE CAVEAT - READ THIS BEFORE USING. Filed at scale "city" to stay inside the
Regime 1 city/region convention, but the actual resolution is COMMUNITY: the
arrondissement is the quartier-equivalent rung. When the community tier is
opened up (Regime 3), this entry should be re-scaled to "community" rather than
duplicated.

WHY IT IS THE FIND OF THE FRENCH WAVE: the four-rung budget ladder asks for a
community rung, and across five French cities this is the ONLY one that exists
as open data. France has no APBDes equivalent - communes are the floor of
fiscal autonomy, and sub-communal bodies (conseils de quartier) generally have
no published budget line. Paris is the exception because the loi PML gives its
arrondissements a statutory delegated budget, so the etat special is a legal
document that must be voted and accounted for.

Consequence for the FCI: the community budget cell is structurally empty in
France except Paris, and that is a finding about French fiscal architecture,
not a gap in the harvest.

Covers the arrondissement's delegated spend only (local facilities,
neighbourhood upkeep) - a small fraction of what is spent in the
arrondissement's territory. Not a territorial spend total.

notes:

ContentsCode, Tid. Region carries 290 values - every Swedish
municipality individually, not size classes. Updated 2026-08-28.

budget is produced by SCB, not by Lund. Same pattern as Quebec (MAMH)
and England (MHCLG): the city rung is served from above. Three
countries in this one wave - it should change where FCI builds

codes and labels as two PARALLEL ARRAYS (values, valueTexts) that must
be zipped POSITIONALLY. Two successive reads of this table during the
harvest returned contradictory pairings - once 1280 to Lund, once
1280/1281/1282 to Vasteras/Sala/Fagersta, a Vastmanland 19xx offset.
Parse by index and ASSERT a known pair (1281 -> Lund) before trusting
any row. A wrong kommunkod puts another city's money under Lund's name.

NOT COFOG. Swedish verksamhetsindelning (RS / kommun-Bas chart of
accounts), 65 areas, no crosswalk found. Sweden runs three unaligned
fiscal classifications across its three live rungs - kommun
verksamhetsomraden, region verksamhetsindelning, 27 statliga
utgiftsomraden. This is Sweden's largest blocker, bigger than any
missing endpoint.

Siblings in the folder: Driftredovisning, InvestKommun (investment by
function, 2015-2025), KopDr (purchased services - a direct
outsourcing / local-sourcing indicator), Lamnadebidrag. OE0107A is the

description:
Per-authority English local government revenue expenditure and
financing from statutory RO returns, 2017-18 to 2024-25, as one CSV
time series on CIPFA SeRCOP service lines. Covers Plymouth.
name: Local authority revenue expenditure and financing England - Revenue Outturn multi-year data set
notes:
Added 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 13, Plymouth).
THE STRONGEST CANDIDATE IN THIS WAVE.

ONE CSV, ~300 ENGLISH CITIES. It solves the Budget|city rung for every
English local authority at once, consistent classification, budget and
outturn together, openly licensed. Plymouth's machine-readable budget
problem is solved by going UP a level, not by parsing council PDFs.
That pattern - Sweden's SCB, Quebec's MAMH, England's MHCLG - holds in
three countries in this wave.

guidance HTML. 2017-18 to 2024-25 in one file. Updated 13 Aug 2026.

UK FISCAL YEAR IS 1 APRIL TO 31 MARCH, as hyphenated pairs. "2024-25"
overlaps calendar 2024 and 2025 and aligns with NEITHER. Comparison
against a calendar-year budget needs an explicit convention, never a
silent cast to the leading year.

Classification: CIPFA SeRCOP service lines plus financing lines
(council tax, business rates retention, grants). NOT COFOG. Line codes
are defined in the 95 KB ODS metadata file - read it. GBP, nominal,
thousands.

UNVERIFIED, WORTH ONE CALL: whether the CSV carries ONS GSS codes or
only MHCLG E-codes. Conventionally both, but the file was not opened.
It determines whether this joins to
governance/city/ons-open-geography-arcgis or needs a lookup table.

What this makes possible and what it does not: a South West figure is
a groupby over authorities whose GSS codes fall in E12000009 -
legitimate as DERIVED data, labelled derived. It is not a published
regional budget, because England has no regional government.

Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated".

description:
Balanced UK regional GDP 1998-2023 in current prices and chained

notes:

description:
The Fab Foundation's directory of fab labs: name, coordinates, activity status
and a six-token capability vocabulary, self-entered by the labs themselves. The
closest thing the network has to a census of where things can be made.
license: NOT OPEN — no data licence published. Platform ToS §7.4 restricts mass harvesting, §7.5 restricts commercial use, §8.1 leaves copyright with each lab. See notes.
name: fablabs.io — Fab Lab Network directory
notes:
NOT OPEN, read anyway by decision. Criterion 1 is unmet; the basis is
recorded and auditable.

DECISION 2026-09-20 — Tomas Diez, co-founder of fablabs.io and of Fab City
Foundation, decided PLANETAI may read this directory and accepted
responsibility, pending the Terms of Use clause drafted the same day. That
covers the Foundation. It does NOT extend to every operator installing a
node: each is a separate party to the ToS. Until the clause lands, a node
reading this relies on one organisation's position, not on a licence.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS SAY. github.com/fablabbcn/fablabs.io is AGPL-3.0 — the Rails
app; neither LICENSE, README nor /about mentions the records. The Terms of Use
at https://fablabs.io/tos govern them, read live 2026-09-20: 7.4 forbids anyone
to "massively collect or harvest" platform data unless they keep all generated
analysis sets open on the Platform; 7.5 forbids commercial use without written
approval; 8.1 leaves copyright with each lab; 8.3 says content published as a
feed lets permitted users use and redistribute it. 8.3 and 7.4/7.5 pull
opposite ways; the document has no open-data provision at all.

RE-READ 2026-09-22, in full, against a reaffirmed decision to proceed. The page
still ends "These Terms of Service was last revised on April 19th 2017" — so the
clause drafted on 20 Sep has NOT landed, and nothing on fablabs.io states a data
licence. 7.4, 7.5, 8.1 as quoted above are intact verbatim. Two further clauses
belong on the record:

7.3 — "You agree not to distribute any part of or parts of the Platform,
including but not limited to any Content, in any medium without Fablabs.io's
prior written authorisation." This is the clause the downstream copies turn on,
not 7.4: economic/community/maps-of-making redistributes 2,412 of these records
and economic/planet/open-hardware-manager serves all of them onward. 7.3 is also
the one a fablabs.io owner CAN settle outright, because the authorisation it
requires is fablabs.io's own to give. One signed sentence covers the chain.

8.2 — the licence labs grant fablabs.io is "solely for the purpose of providing
Platform's services", passable only to those "with whom this latter has
contractual relationships related to the provision of the Platform, solely for
the purpose of providing Platform's services". Read with 8.1, which says
fablabs.io "do not obtain any right, title or interest from you", this is the
limit ownership cannot decide past: an open data licence on the existing records
is not fablabs.io's to grant, because 8.1 says it never received one. That needs
a ToS revision going forward, or the labs. Not a reading to act on without a
lawyer — but it is what the document says.

8.1 is why a footer edit cannot fix this. The fix needing nobody's consent is
scoped to the directory FACTS — name, coordinates, capabilities, status — and
7.4's own exception points there: a node network keeping its analysis open sits
inside it, the ground the decision above stands on.

ENDPOINT: api.fablabs.io/ says the legacy API "has now been removed"; /0/labs.json
returns 200 and 5.38 MB anyway. Both true 2026-09-20. Prefer
economic/community/fablabs-network-data-archive: the same records as pinnable
monthly files.

PRIOR USE: the v0.30 observatory called it from the browser, and
fab-lab-activity-index measures from these records.

MEASURED: 2,864 records, 5.38 MB, 6.3 s; 1,998 active, 1,819 with coordinates.
Query parameters are ignored, so filter client-side. Contact details are
in the payload (email 2,756, phone 2,608) — do not store them.

description:
Forty-eight dated freezes of the fablabs.io lab directory, monthly since 2025,
kept in a public Fab Foundation repository. The same records as the live
endpoint, but pinnable: a dated file instead of a moving target.
license: No licence published — the repository has none, and the records are fablabs.io's, under its Terms of Use. See economic/community/fablabs-io.
name: Fab Lab Network Data — the labs.json archive
notes:
WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM economic/community/fablabs-io: same records,
different access contract. fablabs.io serves a live endpoint that declares
itself removed; this serves dated files in git. Verified 2026-09-20: 48
snapshots from 2018.12.04 to 2026.07.31, monthly since 2025-01, latest 2,828
records and 5.3 MB. Repository actively maintained — commits 2026-09-01
("monthly update") and 2026-09-11, by Pieter van der Hijden.

A PIN, WHICH IS THE POINT. Two nodes reading the same dated file answer
identically; two nodes polling a live endpoint on different days do not. This
is the discipline planetai-node already applies to this very list —
data/sources/REGISTRY_VERSION pins a sha and tools/sync_registry.sh refuses a
branch name, because a floating pin is a node whose answers change under it.
The publisher's own monthly cadence replaces an invented poll interval.

LICENCE — UNCHANGED, AND WORSE THAN IT LOOKS. All 100 paths in the repository
were checked: there is no LICENSE, COPYING or equivalent. The records remain
fablabs.io's, under Terms of Use whose 7.4 forbids anyone "to massively collect
or harvest" platform data. A public repository of 48 complete monthly copies is
that activity, performed by the Foundation's own working group for eight years.
Recorded as fact, not accusation: it is the strongest argument for stating a
licence, because the clause would regularise something the network already
depends on rather than granting anything new.

CARRIES CONTACT DETAILS, like the live endpoint: email on 2,720 of the 2026.07
snapshot, phone on 2,571. Do not store them.

NAMING IS NOT UNIFORM — `2023.03.31 labs.json` uses a space where every other
file uses an underscore, and two files use a `YYYYMMDD_HHMM` form. Anything
globbing this directory must expect both.

`adapter: pack:make` since node v0.70, and that pack ships `MAKE_ENABLED=0`: it
must stay off until the licence is settled. Reading a frozen copy is no more
permitted than reading the live one.

description:
The hackerspace movement's own wiki: 2,601 space pages with structured
coordinates, member counts, equipment and a status vocabulary that records
closures as well as openings. Queryable through Semantic MediaWiki.
name: HackerspaceWiki — List of ALL Hacker Spaces
notes:
LICENCE NOT STATED — and §3's lead of "CC-BY-SA (wiki default)" is wrong. There
is no wiki default here: `api.php?action=query&meta=siteinfo&siprop=rightsinfo`
returns `{"text": "", "url": ""}`, both empty, meaning $wgRightsText and
$wgRightsUrl were never set. A server-side parse of an article carries no licence
line either. MediaWiki says, authoritatively, that this wiki grants nothing.
Criterion 1 is NOT met; licence-pending. A sysop setting two config values fixes
it for 2,601 pages at once.

THE HTML LIST IS BROKEN — do not send anyone to it. `/List_of_ALL_Hacker_Spaces`
returns a PHP fatal error: "Allowed memory size of 67108864 bytes exhausted" in
MediaWiki 1.35.2's QuickTemplate.php. The page is too big for the server's 64 MB
limit. The data is fine; the rendering is not. Use the API.

API VERIFIED 2026-09-22, key-free, at `/w/api.php` (NOT `/api.php`, which the
article rewrite swallows into a 404). Semantic MediaWiki is installed —
`action=smwinfo` reports 171,072 properties — so `action=ask` returns structured
results and bypasses the broken skin entirely.

MEASURED on a 500-row `[[Category:Hackerspace]]` sample of 2,601 pages: has
coordinates 403, `Hackerspace status` 497, `Number of members` 361, `Equipment`
161, `SpaceAPI` 28. The property names are `Has coordinates` and `Hackerspace
status` — not `Coordinates` or `Status`, which return zero rows and look like
missing data.

COUNT THE STATUSES. Of 500: active 183, closed 124, suspected inactive 66,
planned 65, building 43, reformatting 8, unknown 8. **Only 37% are active**, so
a node reading 2,601 pages without filtering will route somebody to a space that
shut down. That the wiki records closures at all makes it better curated than the
aggregators that copy from it.

28 spaces carry a `SpaceAPI` property pointing at their own live endpoint — the
join to economic/community/spaceapi-directory.

No `adapter`: nothing in planetai-node reads it yet.

national geometry. A bioregion that is not a country can only be
approximated by downscaling national per-capita values by population,
which is an assumption and not data. Ecological footprint and
biocapacity are two of the most Fab-City-native indicators in the
framework and this is the weakest slicing path in the environmental row
- the index should state the downscaling assumption explicitly rather
than carry it silently.

mirror. Best-in-class slicing: global 30 m raster clipped to any
polygon. /dataset/wwf_terrestrial_ecoregions also exists and is
downloadable but its source and license fields returned null - establish

description:
Global vector polygons of sub-basin boundaries, hierarchically nested
across 12 levels with Pfafstetter coding and upstream/downstream
topology. About 1.0 million sub-basin polygons covering 135 million
square kilometres.
license: HydroSHEDS license — free for scientific, educational and commercial use with attribution
name: HydroSHEDS — HydroBASINS
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09. THIS IS THE SLICING INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT AN
INDICATOR. It is what makes 'bioregion' a computable object: pick a
Pfafstetter level (4-6 is typically bioregion-sized, 5-8 for a Fab City
catchment), take the polygon, and use it to clip every raster in the
environmental row and to spatially join every point dataset. Pairs
directly with Caravan (already listed), with Aqueduct's sub-basin units,
and with the TFDD transboundary basin layer in the governance row.
Commercial use is explicitly permitted, which is rare across this
harvest and makes it safe as the index's public boundary layer. Static
reference layer, v1, no update cadence.

notes:
Verified 2026-09-09. REST API IS DEGRADED - do not rely on it. Three
calls to rest.isric.org/soilgrids/v2.0/properties/query with different
coordinates all returned well-formed JSON with values.mean = null, and
ISRIC's own site carries a notice that the REST API is unavailable due
to technical issues. Use the file services instead: WCS at
maps.isric.org (designed for bounding-box subsetting and the recommended
path for modelling pipelines) or WebDAV/VRT at
files.isric.org/soilgrids/latest/data/. Full downloads are ~5 GB per map
and ~120 GB per property, so WCS subsetting is not optional.
METHODOLOGICAL CAVEAT: these are model predictions, not measurements,
with no time dimension. The framework's 'soil health index' implies
observed condition and trend; SoilGrids gives a static modelled property
surface. It is a proxy and the index should say so.

description:

license: CC-BY-4.0 (Open-Meteo) with mandatory attribution to the model providers (DWD, ECMWF, Meteo-France, NCEP)
name: Open-Meteo Marine Weather API
notes:

nearest ocean cell, so inland nodes get a cell that may be far away.

ocean cell is further than COAST_MAX_KM (default 30). Free for
non-commercial use; commercial use needs an Open-Meteo subscription.

PLANETAI: `packs/coast` samples the nearest ocean cell onto `marine-point`, and `packs/posidonia`
reads those same rows against a thermal-stress threshold. Both land on `Environmental|Bioregion`,
which is why `feeds_cells` carries one key and not two.
`auth: none` records what a node must hold — nothing. The non-commercial limit in `license` is a
separate question and stays there; a node operator, not this file, decides it.

notes:

Check station presence per bioregion before promising this indicator
anywhere.

notes:

https://files.wri.org/aqueduct/aqueduct-4-0-water-risk-data.zip.

ENVIRONMENTAL ROW: Aqueduct is published on hydrological sub-basin units
plus country and province aggregates, so a bioregion defined as a
watershed maps almost directly onto Aqueduct polygons - join on basin ID
or spatial intersect. The native unit is already a hydrological unit,
which no other source in this row can say. Caveat on water quality:
Aqueduct's quality indicators are coefficient-of-variation and
untreated-wastewater proxies, not measured concentrations - pair with
GEMStat for actual measurements. Baseline period roughly 1979-2019;
major-version releases rather than continuous updates.

description:

Classified at city scale: 10 m pixels are far finer than a bioregion needs
and it is the land layer a municipality or a lab can actually use.

notes:

through CDP. Baseline 1990; targets -30% by 2020, -55% by 2030.

Compare with the alternatives found in the same wave: Finland's SYKE
uses the national ALas/Hinku method with no GPC mapping, and the UK's
DESNZ series is territorial with aviation, shipping and F-gases
excluded. Montreal is the one that arrives already in the schema FCI
wants. Where a GPC-versus-national-method comparison has to be made,
use Montreal as the reference implementation.

TRAPS. (1) TEN CSVs - one per sector per language, FR and EN pairs
with DIFFERENT COLUMN HEADERS. A connector must union five files and
pick a language, not glob the directory. (2) Inventory years are
IRREGULAR - Montreal has historically published every 2-3 years
despite an "annual" cadence on the page; the actual year list was not
confirmed. (3) Baseline 1990 restatements are common in GPC
inventories; do not assume a fixed back-series.

Files last modified roughly two years before this harvest, so the
cadence caveat is not theoretical.

Same portal licence inference as montreal-budget-fonctionnement.

description:
Hourly air quality index per monitoring station from Montreal's RSQA
network, covering SO2, CO, O3, NO2 and PM2.5. Published as a rolling
daily CSV, updated about ten minutes past each hour.
name: RSQA - Indice de la qualite de l'air, temps reel (Montreal)
notes:
Added 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 13, Montreal).
Publisher: Service de l'environnement et de la transition ecologique.
Resources showed "last updated 6 minutes ago" at fetch time.

THE PUBLISHED VALUE IS AN INDEX, NOT A CONCENTRATION. IQA is
(measurement / reference value) x 50, banded Bon 1-25, Acceptable
26-50, Mauvais 51+. If the FCI wants PM2.5 in ug/m3 you must invert
the formula using the reference values, or go to the separate
rsqa-bilans-annuels-qualite-air dataset. Do not plot IQA as if it were
a concentration.

THREE MORE TRAPS. (1) Station coordinates and sector live in a
SEPARATE dataset, donnees.montreal.ca/dataset/rsqa-liste-des-stations
- you must join. (2) Two near-identical CSVs are offered, "IQA
detaille par station" and "IQA par station"; pick deliberately.
(3) The file is a DAILY SNAPSHOT THAT ROLLS. There is no API and no
history in the resource - a connector must poll and accumulate or it
loses the series permanently.

Same portal licence inference as montreal-budget-fonctionnement.

description:
Reference-grade air quality aggregator. Pulls from ~10k+ regulatory
monitoring stations globally and harmonises to a common schema.
Free public API with optional auth for higher rate limits.
name: OpenAQ
notes:
v3 API recommends API key for production use. Bbox queries are the
fastest filter. Combine with Sensor.Community for community-tier
density layer, with Smart Citizen for community-deployed sensors.

description:
The Dutch national air quality monitoring network, run by RIVM with regional
environment agencies. Open JSON API serving station metadata and hourly
concentrations for NO2, PM10, PM2.5, O3 and more.
name: Luchtmeetnet / Landelijk Meetnet Luchtkwaliteit (RIVM)
notes:
Verified 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 10). The open API was
called, not just read about: /open_api/stations?page=1 returns a paginated
JSON list, 25 stations per page across 5 pages - roughly 125 stations
nationally, each with an "NL"-prefixed number and a location string.

LICENCE is CC-BY (4.0), read from the national register record for the
hourly series, data.overheid.nl/dataset/27136-meetwaarden-landelijk-meetnet-
luchtkwaliteit--rivm---uur, published by RIVM through CBS. The Luchtmeetnet
site's own open-data page does not print a licence, so the register record
is the authority here.

TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, DON'T CONFUSE THEM. api.luchtmeetnet.nl is the live
and recent-history API, no key needed. The VALIDATED annual series is a
separate product: RIVM StatLine table 50084NED, OData at
dataderden.cbs.nl/ODataCatalog/, published in Q2 for the previous year, data
from 2012 onward. Live for dashboards, validated for indicators.

Filed at city scale because stations sit in and report for individual
municipalities, which is where the atomic measurement happens - the same
rule this list applies to community-tier sensor networks.

/open_api (the bare path) returned HTTP 500 on 2026-09-11; the documented
entry point api-docs.luchtmeetnet.nl is what to use.

description:
Citizen-science air quality sensor network rooted in Germany,
active across the EU. ~30k SDS011-based PM sensors with public API
and bulk archive download.
name: Sensor.Community
notes:
Formerly known as luftdaten.info. Coverage densest in Germany,
Belgium, Netherlands, Poland; non-trivial in Spain (especially
Barcelona). Bulk archive available at archive.sensor.community.
Complements Smart Citizen well: SDS011 sensors are cheaper and
more numerous; Smart Citizen kits carry more parameters.

description: Daily-average air quality index, PM10, ozone, NO2, CO and SO2 for Seoul, with a series running from 1987 to 2025. The ~38-year depth is exceptional for an urban air-quality record.
license: 공공누리 1유형 : 출처표시 (상업적 이용 및 변경 가능) - KOGL Type 1
name: Seoul Daily Average Air Environment Information (서울시 기간별 일평균 대기환경 정보)
notes:

Read in a browser, not inferred from a status code: the page 404s to any client without Javascript, so a link checker cannot tell this apart from a portal that simply dislikes scripts. A replacement should be found by searching 열린데이터광장 for a successor id, not by trusting this one.
Verified 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 12). Cadence 비정기(수시).

ACCESS LIMIT: the sheet and Open API return ONLY the most recent 1 year. The
historic series needs the file route.

PM2.5 and per-자치구 breakdown are NOT in this dataset - they live in siblings
OA-1200 (실시간 자치구별), OA-2221, OA-2275, OA-15526, OA-2218, OA-2219, whose

WHY THE CITY SOURCE AND NOT THE NATIONAL ONE: the national AirKorea API
(data.go.kr/data/15073861) does expose PM2.5 and is richer, but it is licensed
공공저작물 : 출처표시, 변경금지 (제 3유형) - KOGL Type 3, NO DERIVATIVES - which
makes it unusable for an index that computes derived indicators. Seoul's own
family is KOGL Type 1. This is the clearest case in the wave where the national
source is restricted and the city source is not.

description: Seoul's annual greenhouse gas inventory split by direct and indirect emissions, published by the city's Climate and Environment Bureau. Companion dataset OA-21081 gives the same inventory broken out by sector.
license: 공공누리 1유형 : 출처표시 (상업적 이용 및 변경 가능) - KOGL Type 1
name: Seoul GHG Inventory by Direct/Indirect (서울시 온실가스 인벤토리 직간접별 현황)
notes:
DEPRECATED 2026-09-19. The dataset page now returns the termination notice the portal itself renders — 서비스 종료 안내 / 해당 데이터는 종료된 서비스입니다, "this data is a terminated service". Verified 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 12). Owner 기후환경본부
기후환경정책과. Cadence 년간. Sheet (1,000-row cap) + CSV + Open API.

CAUTION: the dataset page displayed 「파일이 없습니다」 (no file present) at the
time of check. The metadata record is live and current, but the attachment may

NO GPC AND NO IPCC PROTOCOL is referenced on the page, so GPC conformance
cannot be claimed for this inventory. The Fab City Index Environmental|City GHG

Sub-city granularity exists elsewhere but not openly: energyinfo.seoul.go.kr
publishes GHG by 자치구 and energy source with an Excel download and NO licence,

description:
Hourly XML feed from Slovenia's national air quality network - 24
stations, three of them in Ljubljana, reporting PM10, PM2.5, NO2, O3,
SO2, benzene, CO and NOx with coordinates and elevation.
name: ARSO hourly air quality measurements (Slovenia)
notes:
Added 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 13, Ljubljana).

VERIFIED BY DIRECT FETCH. Root element arsopodatki, repeating postaja
elements each carrying merilno_mesto (station name), datum_od /
datum_do, D96 and WGS84 coordinates, elevation, and pollutant children
co, o3, no2, pm10, pm2.5, benzen, nox, so2. 24 stations nationally.
The three Ljubljana stations are LJ Bezigrad, LJ Celovska, LJ Vic.
PM2.5 is present on 20 of the 24 stations - absent on MB Vrbanski, CE
Ljubljanska, MS Cankarjeva and Krvavec, so do not assume full PM2.5
coverage of the network.

THREE TRAPS. (1) THE ELEMENT NAME IS <pm2.5> - A DOT IN THE TAG NAME.
That breaks naive XPath and several XML-to-dict libraries. This is the
single most likely thing to make a connector fail on day one.
(2) THE FEED IS "ZADNJI" - LAST HOURS ONLY. There is no history in it.
A connector must poll and accumulate or the series is lost. (3)
STATION NAMES ARE THE JOIN KEY, NOT CODES. Free-text names mean
entity-resolution work if you ever join to another source.

LICENCE IS PUBLISHER-LEVEL INFERENCE, FLAGGED. ARSO's OPSI publisher
page shows 75 datasets, of which 44 carry "Priznanje avtorstva (CC BY
4.0)" and 31 carry other terms which were not retrieved verbatim. The
air-quality dataset "Podatki o kakovosti zunanjega zraka in padavin"
is listed there but WHICH of the two regimes applies to THIS FEED was
not confirmed. Re-verify before redistribution. ARSO's format
distribution is poor by openness rating - 31 datasets at zero stars,
41 at one star - so do not read the CC BY share as a sign of a
well-run open data estate.

The feed fetched on 2026-09-11 carried a 2026-09-04 timestamp, i.e.
about a week stale at read time. Status remains live, but a connector
should check freshness rather than trusting the "urni" label.

description:
Per-municipality and per-region GHG emissions by sector for Finland
under the ALas/Hinku model - electricity, heating, transport, industry,
agriculture, waste - downloadable as Excel tables. Run by SYKE.
name: SYKE municipal and regional greenhouse gas emissions (ALas)
notes:
Added 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 13, Oulu). Covers
Oulu at city scale and Pohjois-Pohjanmaa at region scale in the same
service.

NOT GPC. This is the Finnish national ALas/Hinku method, with three
calculation variants (Hinku calculation, Hinku without credits, all
emissions). GPC scope 1/2/3 mapping is not provided and is not
trivially derivable. Any FCI GHG indicator built on this is not
directly comparable with a GPC city like Montreal, which publishes
GPC reference numbers per row.

API IS NULL DELIBERATELY. The page offers "Lataa tiedot
Excel-taulukkoina" but the municipality selector is JavaScript-driven
and no direct download URL was exposed in the rendered content. Do not
infer one. The download path has to be recovered from a browser
session before a connector can be built.

LICENCE IS ONE STEP OF INFERENCE, FLAGGED. The paastot page states no
licence. SYKE's institutional page
(syke.fi/en/environmental-data/open-web-services) states verbatim:
"Syke applies Creative Commons By 4.0 International license for open
datasets and map services." The institutional licence is carried
across to this service. Re-verify before any redistribution.

description:
Per-authority and regional waste tonnage, recycling rates and
household waste per person for England, 2024/25 with a back-series to
2012-13, published as ODS spreadsheets from WasteDataFlow returns.
name: Local authority collected waste management - annual results (England)
notes:
Added 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 13, Plymouth).

Like the DESNZ GHG release, ONE FILE SERVES CITY AND REGION:
LA_and_Regional_Spreadsheet_2024-25.ods (2.04 MB) carries the regional
aggregation explicitly alongside per-authority rows. Companion
WFH_England_Data_202425.ods (49 KB) covers household waste. Includes
"Collected household waste per person (kg)".

FORMAT IS ODS, NOT CSV. OpenDocument Spreadsheet. Many CSV-first
pipelines and some pandas configurations will not read it without
odfpy. Budget for a conversion step across the whole DEFRA series.
Multi-sheet workbooks with header banners above the data rectangle -
THE FIRST ROW IS NOT THE HEADER ROW.

WASTE-AUTHORITY STRUCTURE VARIES ACROSS ENGLAND and this will bite a
generic connector. Two-tier areas split waste between a collection
authority and a disposal authority, so tonnage arrives in two rows
under two bodies. PLYMOUTH IS A UNITARY - it is both, so its row is
complete. Do not generalise Plymouth's completeness to other English
cities without checking their tier.

Financial-year labelled (2024/25 = April-March), consistent with the
budget rung. Underlying collection system is WasteDataFlow, which has
its own data.gov.uk record that was not fetched.

Licence verbatim: "All content is available under the Open Government
Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated".

description:
Annual territorial GHG emissions for every UK local authority and
region, 2005-2024, as an 82.6 MB CSV plus Excel tables. Excludes
aviation, shipping, military transport and fluorinated gases.
name: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics
notes:
Added 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 13, Plymouth).

ONE FILE SERVES CITY AND REGION. The release is titled "local
authority AND regional" and publishes both levels together, so the
Environmental|City and Environmental|Region cells are one ingest, not
two. Not duplicated as a separate region entry for that reason. A
useful property of the England data estate and worth checking for in
other countries.

THE EXCLUSION LIST IS THE WHOLE STORY FOR A PORT CITY. Verbatim from
the page: "All emissions included in the national inventory are
covered except those from aviation, shipping and military transport,
for which there is no obvious basis for allocation to local areas, and
emissions of fluorinated gases, for which suitable data are not
available to estimate these emissions at a local level." PLYMOUTH IS A
MAJOR NAVAL AND FERRY PORT. Its GHG figure from this source is
systematically incomplete in precisely the sector where Plymouth is
atypical, and comparing it to an inland city compares unlike things.
Surface the exclusion in the indicator; do not bury it.

SECOND FRAMING PROBLEM: these are TERRITORIAL / PRODUCTION emissions,
not consumption-based. A Fab City framing that cares about material
and consumption footprints wants the opposite basis, and this dataset
cannot supply it. Compare
environmental/city/montreal-ges-collectivite-gpc, which at least
carries GPC scopes.

TRAPS. The 82.6 MB CSV is a flat long file across 2005-2024 x all UK
LAs x all sectors - server-side filtering is impossible, so a
connector must stream-filter on the GSS code. GSS keying is ASSERTED,
not verified; the page does not state it and the CSV was not opened.

Licence verbatim: "All content is available under the Open Government
Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated".

description:
Inventory of Zagreb's urban air-quality monitoring stations - location,
substances measured, operating institution and competent authority - served
as CSV, GeoJSON, KML and SHP from the city's ArcGIS Hub.
name: Geoportal Kvaliteta zraka Grada Zagreba
notes:
Verified 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 10). Last modified
2026-04-15. Update frequency: not scheduled.

READ THE SCOPE CAREFULLY. This is the STATION INVENTORY, not the
measurements. It answers "where does Zagreb measure air, and what does each
station measure" - which is the station-density half of the Environmental|
City air-quality indicator - and nothing about concentrations.

For actual Zagreb concentration values the closest open-licensed find in
this pass was data.gov.hr/ckan/dataset/cd4810c8-0888-4b78-b324-05185a4eb349
"Podaci o kvaliteti zraka u Gradu Zagrebu - Ksaver 2023", CC-BY, eight
monthly XLSX files - one station, one year. Croatia's national network is
published by the environment agency as INSPIRE WMS/WFS at
servisi.azo.hr/inspire/geos1/ with no licence stated on the catalogue
record, so it is not listed here.

Despite the data.gov.hr URL this is a Grad Zagreb dataset; the city
registers it nationally but hosts the files on ArcGIS Hub.

description:
Open-hardware indoor + outdoor air quality monitoring network with
public REST API. PM2.5, PM10, CO2, TVOC, NOx, temperature, humidity.
~10k+ devices deployed globally; transparent pricing for the open
variant.
name: AirGradient
notes:
Strong fit for the Community-tier indoor environment signal that
Smart Citizen does not cover well (Smart Citizen focuses outdoor).
AirGradient kits are commonly deployed in schools, offices, and homes.
Combined with Smart Citizen they form a complementary indoor + outdoor
community sensing layer.

description:
Island-wide PM2.5 archive for Bali aggregating eight sensor networks
(Nafas, IQAir, PurpleAir, AQICN, OpenAQ, AirGradient, Smart Citizen, Airly)
into one key-free, read-only API with raw and humidity-corrected values.
license: Public-interest archive; redistribution encouraged with attribution to Bali Air Dispatch and to the originating network named in each row. Upstream readings remain under their networks' terms.
name: Bali Air Dispatch
notes:
A peer observatory, not a sensor network: credit both the archive and the
row's network. Endpoints: /stations, /latest, /measurements (raw, hourly,
daily; JSON or CSV). Applies the US EPA 2021 humidity correction to
Plantower-based networks and stores raw alongside corrected; flags
suspected-indoor stations and stale readings. Collaborators: Fab Lab Bali,
CAST Foundation, Bali Net Zero Coalition, Meaningful Design Group.
PLANETAI: read by `app/sources.py::baliairdispatch()` as reference context
(local=false) on Bali nodes and by `packs/nearby`. Nodes with outdoor
hardware should also publish to a network BAD reads so the map densifies.

PLANETAI: three readers, and `adapter` names one. `app/sources.py::baliairdispatch()` ingests the ring;
`packs/nearby` configures and verifies it; `packs/season` reads the same rows over a 68-day window.
Its stations are stored `local=False`, so they fill the public-reference-stations cell and never the
in-custody one — which is the whole point of the ring.

description:
Community species observation platform. ~200M+ research-grade
observations globally with photo verification by community
identifiers. Used as the de facto biodiversity citizen-science layer.
name: iNaturalist
notes:
Wired in PLANETAI observatory. Note: per-observation licenses vary;
~50% of records are CC-BY-NC, ~25% CC0, rest restricted. Use the
/observations endpoint with `licensed=true` to filter to redistributable
records.

description:
Open-hardware community sensor network from Fab Lab Barcelona / IAAC.
~25k kits deployed globally measuring PM2.5, sound, temperature, humidity,
light, CO2. FOSS hardware + firmware, public REST API.
name: Smart Citizen
notes:
Originated at Fab Lab Barcelona / IAAC. Public devices endpoint:
/devices/world_map (returns ~50-100k device records).
Per-device readings: /devices/{id}/readings.
Used as the canonical Community-tier environmental signal in the
PLANETAI observatory. Note: BCN archive is ~98% dormant
(25 of 1,408 kits actively reporting as of April 2026).
Fab labs can deploy kits and contribute to the network with no
enrollment friction. Kit ID #19236 is the live anchor used in
the observatory's Local view.

description:
Earth-system foundation model from Microsoft Research. Hourly
forecasts to 14 days for atmosphere, ocean wave, and air quality
state. Model weights released under MIT.
license: MIT (model weights); CDS license for ERA5 training inputs
name: Microsoft Aurora
notes:
Not an API but a model checkpoint. PLANETAI uses pre-computed
Aurora forecasts as the C0-C3 planet-tier panels. Compute cost
for inference is non-trivial — published forecasts via partners
like Climate Engine or running on Azure HPC are the typical path.
Compare with GraphCast (Google DeepMind) and GenCast (Google DeepMind).

description:
Uniformly calibrated global open-ocean data product of inorganic carbon
variables including DIC, total alkalinity and pH, merged from research
cruises. Maintained by GEOMAR and the ICOS Ocean Thematic Centre,
archived at NOAA NCEI.
license: Website content CC-BY-4.0; the data product is gated behind a Data Use Statement — data license UNCONFIRMED
name: GLODAP v2.2023 — Global Ocean Data Analysis Project
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09. Regional and merged master files as zipped CSV via
NOAA NCEI OCADS and a GEOMAR mirror. Coverage roughly 1970s-2021
depending on basin; releases are irregular (roughly annual to biennial),
no fixed cadence stated. LICENSE ACTION REQUIRED: the site asks users to
review a separate Data Use Statement that was not fetched, so do not
assume CC BY for the data itself. SLICING: point observations with
lat/lon/depth, so filter by bounding box or clip to a marine polygon.
Basin-level slicing is reliable because Atlantic/Pacific/Indian/Arctic
files ship pre-split. Bioregion-level is NOT reliable: coverage is
cruise-based and spatially uneven, so many coastal bioregions will have
zero or sparse points. Report N alongside any derived value.

description:
Riverine flood forecasts up to 7 days ahead for ~80 countries
including Indonesia, Spain, Chile. Inundation maps + alerts via
free public API (rate-limited).
name: Google Flood Hub
notes:
Coverage is not uniform — basins included are listed in the
/gauges endpoint. Bali has limited but non-zero coverage;
Spain has good Mediterranean coverage; Chile coverage is
partial. Boston / NE US is excluded. Complement with Caravan
hydrology dataset for basin-scale modelling.

description:
NASA GISS land-ocean surface temperature anomaly analysis. Global,
hemispheric and zonal CSV tables plus 2x2 degree gridded NetCDF and Zarr
anomaly fields relative to a 1951-1980 baseline.
license: No formal license — acknowledgement expected; credit NASA GISS/GISTEMP
name: NASA GISTEMP v4 — surface temperature analysis
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09. Updated around the 10th of every month, covering
1880-present. Verified file URLs: tabledata_v4/GLB.Ts+dSST.csv and
ZonAnn.Ts+dSST.csv; gridded gistemp1200_GHCNv4_ERSSTv5.nc.gz (2 degree,
1200 km smoothing) and gistemp250_GHCNv4.nc.gz (250 km); Zarr v3
directories under /pub/gistemp/. TWO SLICING PATHS: the CSV tables give
global, hemispheric and zonal bands only, with no bioregional path; the
gridded NetCDF/Zarr can be clipped to a bioregion polygon and area-
weighted. At 2 degrees (~220 km) a small bioregion falls inside one or
two cells, so the gridded route is good for a trend line and not for
intra-bioregion variation. Copernicus CDS
(cds.climate.copernicus.eu/api, token required, server-side bounding-box
subsetting) is the higher-resolution alternative if 2 degrees proves too
coarse.

description:
NASA Langley's Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources: solar and
meteorological parameters from MERRA-2 and CERES, hourly to climatology,
for any point on Earth since 1981, via a key-free REST API.
license: US Government work (public domain); NASA POWER asks for citation
name: NASA POWER
notes:
Temporal endpoints: hourly, daily, monthly, climatology, each as
/api/temporal/{level}/point?parameters=...&latitude=&longitude=&community=RE|AG|SB.
Resolution ~0.5 x 0.625 deg (MERRA-2); a point query returns the enclosing cell.
PLANETAI: `app/bootstrap.py::power_climatology()` pulls the 12 monthly
normals (temperature, humidity, solar, precipitation) for the node's
coordinates at first start; the `cold-start` pack cites this slug. It is
the reason a node needs coordinates, not a sensor, to have a baseline.

`feeds_cells` is empty on purpose: the twelve monthly normals land on `power-point`, `kind='model'`,
as `*_norm` metrics that no cells.yml reads. They are what a normal year looks like here — the
baseline a measurement is read against, not a measurement.

description:
NOAA GML's canonical atmospheric CO2 record: Mauna Loa daily, weekly and
monthly means plus the globally averaged marine surface annual mean,
from the NOAA cooperative air sampling network.
license: No formal license — freely available to the public and the scientific community; citation requested
name: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory — CO2 trends
notes:
Verified 2026-09-09 by fetching the data file itself:
https://gml.noaa.gov/webdata/ccgg/trends/co2/co2_annmean_gl.txt returns
columns year, mean, unc, first row 1979 = 336.85 ppm, last row 2023 =
419.31 ppm, file stamped July 2024. The .csv variants are blocked by
robots.txt - use the .txt files, which are the reliable harvest path.
Stable flat-file URLs under /webdata/ccgg/trends/co2/:
co2_annmean_gl.txt, co2_mm_mlo.txt, co2_daily_mlo.txt, co2_gr_mlo.txt.
SLICING: none needed. This is a single global scalar per time step - a
planetary constant that every bioregion shares, which makes it the
cheapest cell in the whole matrix to fill. NOAA notes coauthorship for
data providers may be appropriate for research use.

description:
Free weather + climate API with no auth required. Backed by ECMWF +
GFS + DWD + KNMI. Hourly forecasts to 14 days, historical reanalysis,
climate projections, marine forecasts.
name: Open-Meteo
notes:
Most generous free tier in the weather-API space. Used for
geocoding (forward + reverse), climate projections, marine
forecasts, and as a fallback for several PLANETAI panels.
Reverse-geocoding via /v1/forecast carries city + country names
so it doubles as a geocoder.

`feeds_cells` is empty on purpose: `openmeteo()` writes `temp_model`, `humidity_model` and friends
to `om-point`, `kind='model'`, and no pack's cells.yml reads those metrics. It is a boundary
condition and a geocoder, never aggregated upward into a cell.

description:
Key-free hourly air-quality forecasts and 92 days of history from the
Copernicus CAMS global (0.4 deg) and European (0.1 deg) models: PM2.5,

name: Dados Abertos Recife
notes:

single value, "Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL)", on 222 of 222
datasets. No unspecified remainder, unlike Belo Horizonte or Boston.

the action API docs, but /api/3/action/* on this host is disallowed by
robots.txt, so it is not available to a well-behaved client. Same call as the
Boston entry: catalogue enumeration has to come from rendered HTML. Ignoring
robots is a deliberate choice, not a default.

PUBLISHERS by volume: Secretaria de Saude 62, CTTU (transito e transporte) 30,
Secretaria de Educacao 26, Secretaria de Meio Ambiente e Sustentabilidade 12,
SEDUL 9, Secretaria de Infraestrutura 9, Secretaria de Financas 8, EMLURB

GROUPS: saude 65, urbanismo 25, mobilidade 23, governo e politica 15, covid 11,

IPTU and ITBI - property and transfer taxes, which are revenue instruments, not
a budget. No orcamento / despesas / receitas dataset surfaced in the catalogue
facets, and no licitacoes or contratos register either. Recife's budget rung is

description:
Gemeente Amsterdam's data catalogue and its DataPunt REST API, which serves
roughly 100 versioned dataset collections (BAG, trees, ecology, waste,
gas-free zones) as JSON, plus WFS and MVT layers.
name: Amsterdam Open Data / DataPunt API
notes:
Verified 2026-09-11 in the FCI Regime 1 harvest (wave 10).
https://api.data.amsterdam.nl/v1/ returns a JSON service index: one entry
per dataset with versioned and unversioned endpoints, status "stabiel", and
an authorisation field that is "OPENBAAR" for most and restricted for a few.

LICENCE. The catalogue's own pages do not print a licence. Amsterdam's
records on the national portal do: data.overheid.nl shows CC-0 (1.0) for
Gemeente Amsterdam datasets (checked on /dataset/aiwltsev_igoxa). Recorded
as CC0-1.0 on that basis, which is one step of inference - if a specific
dataset matters, check its own record rather than trusting this header.

API KEYS ARE COMING. The v1 docs say key registration is optional now and
becomes mandatory at a later deadline. An unauthenticated connector built
today will break. Plan for a key.

THE DCAT ENDPOINT IS GONE. api.data.amsterdam.nl/dcatd/datasets - the path
the Amsterdam/dcatd repo documents - returns 404 as of 2026-09-11. Use the

NO CITY BUDGET HERE. A catalogue search for "begroting" surfaced no budget
dataset. Amsterdam's municipal finances reach open data through the national
